companyFounding.title: Found your first company
companyFounding.description: Hire a CEO, set up a runtime and model service, create company documents — until your first engineer can start work.

firstProjectPractice.title: First project practice: Classic Snake
firstProjectPractice.description: Walk a trimmed-down Snake project through the full loop: requirements, design, development, testing, acceptance and delivery. Skippable, and restartable later.

library.title: Tutorial center
library.description: The core tutorial walks you through setting up the company — every step is real work. The project practice is optional and you can come back anytime.
library.skipConfirmBody: No project is created, no AI employee is called, and no model fees are charged. You can restart it anytime.
library.skippedWithCost: Skipped: no project was created and nothing was charged.

practice.dialogBody: Your AI employees will run this project for real, from requirements through to delivery.
practice.accelerated: Accelerated mode: a trimmed-down demo project — the full process, with less content.
practice.usesLlm: These employees use real model services, so running the project incurs model fees.
practice.mockOnly: Every employee runs on a mock runtime, so there are no model fees.
practice.noEmployees: No employee is ready to work yet. Finish the runtime and model service steps in the core tutorial first.
practice.mockOption: Want to see the flow without spending anything?
practice.mockOptionHint: Switch the employee runtime to Mock, then come back and start the practice.

handoff.title: Your company can run now
handoff.body: The CEO and the engineer are ready. Want to take a trimmed-down Snake project through the full loop, from requirements to delivery?

company_setup.label: Your company is empty for now
company_setup.explanation: You are about to build it yourself: hire people, set up their tools, and ship the first project.

hire_ceo.label: Hire your first CEO
hire_ceo.explanation: The company's first employee, responsible for decisions and management. Project reviews and task assignments go through him.
hire_ceo.why: Without a CEO, nobody owns project reviews and the flow stalls.

configure_ceo_runtime.label: Give the CEO a runtime
configure_ceo_runtime.explanation: The runtime is his work environment — it decides how he works and which tools he uses. Start with Mock to try the flow for free, then switch to a real runtime for real work.
configure_ceo_runtime.why: Identity, runtime and model are separate: you can change models without hiring a new employee.

configure_ceo_provider.label: Connect the CEO to a model service
configure_ceo_provider.explanation: Pick a model service, enter the key and the model you want. Without a key he cannot start work.
configure_ceo_provider.why: A service without a stored key looks configured but fails on the first run.

configure_company_resources.label: Set up workspace and access
configure_company_resources.explanation: Eidolon creates his workspace and document space automatically, and assigns permissions by role. The Git account can wait until later.
configure_company_resources.why: The workspace holds code, the document space holds material, and permissions decide what he can touch — this is where his output lands.

cloud_docs.label: Write the first company document
cloud_docs.explanation: The company needs a shared knowledge base. Write anything — a charter, a plan, your first idea.

git_setup.label: Connect a code repository
git_setup.explanation: Code needs somewhere to live. Install the built-in Git service if you have none, or connect GitLab or GitHub Enterprise.

hire_engineer.label: Hire your first engineer
hire_engineer.explanation: Now hire someone to do the work. Same flow as before: identity, runtime, model and permissions in one pass.
hire_engineer.why: The CEO decides and the engineer delivers. With both roles in place, the company can actually run.

configure_engineer.label: Make sure the engineer can take work
configure_engineer.explanation: Four things must be ready: active identity, a runtime, a working model connection, and a workspace.
configure_engineer.why: Missing any one of them stalls assigned tasks. Use the same four checks when you hire the next person.

hire_qa.label: Do you want a QA too?
hire_qa.explanation: A QA hunts for problems and makes delivery steadier. You can skip it for now — the project will keep reminding you that the engineer is testing his own work.

create_project.label: Kick off the first project
create_project.explanation: Build a playable Snake game. The requirements form is already filled in from the sample — review it and approve to start.

requirements_review.label: Confirm the requirements
requirements_review.explanation: The team has broken the requirements down. Review them and approve. Design and development will follow them from here.
requirements_review.why: Changing requirements is cheap now. After work starts, design, code and tests all have to be redone.

design_review.label: See how they plan to build it
design_review.explanation: System design, the presentation and the speaker notes are all here. Approve the plan to move into development.
design_review.why: This is the last cheap gate before work starts — catching problems now costs far less than fixing them in code.

development.label: Watch the engineer work
development.explanation: See which files changed, what was committed and how far along the work is — no black box.

testing.label: Self-test, then verify against acceptance criteria
testing.explanation: The team finds and fixes its own issues first, then checks every acceptance criterion in the requirements. The test report ships with the delivery.

acceptance_review.label: The final call is yours
acceptance_review.explanation: The build, the evidence and the reports are all here. Your sign-off is what makes it deliverable.
acceptance_review.why: AI can prepare every piece of evidence, but the decision to hand it to a customer stays with you — that is the last human check before delivery.

delivery.label: Package the delivery
delivery.explanation: Code, build, manuals, release notes and meeting minutes — organised in one pass, ready to hand over or archive.

hints.identity: Start with identity: name, role and reporting line.
hints.pickRuntime: Pick a runtime. Use Mock to try the flow for free, then switch to a real one for real work.
hints.pickProvider: Enter the model service key and model — that is what lets him start working.
hints.pickAccess: Tick the access packages. The workspace, document space and Git account are created here.
hints.engineerAccess: The engineer follows the same flow — this hint only calls out what differs from the CEO.
hints.confirmOnboard: Submit to hire him. Eidolon then creates his runtime and workspace.
hints.openRuntimeTab: Switch to the Runtime tab first — the binding lives there.
hints.bindProvider: Create the model service here with its key and model, and the binding is done in one go.
hints.intakeBasic: Basic info is pre-filled: name, code, priority, customer, owner and deadline. Just confirm the owner is the person you want.
hints.intakePurpose: Background and objectives are filled in too — this is the problem the project solves. Continue when it looks right.
hints.intakeRequirements: All seven structured requirements are listed, each with acceptance criteria. Edit any of them or move on.
hints.intakeDelivery: Technical requirements, constraints, deliverables and milestones are filled in. Confirm the scope looks right.
hints.intakeReviews: The three mandatory reviews are fixed. Add optional reviews if you like, and pick a customer contact and presenter.
hints.intakeConfirm: Last check: submitting really creates the project and starts the lifecycle. Click “Create project”.
